title: Correct acceleration magnitude
description: Essential: The final numerical magnitude of the acceleration must be 300 m/s².

title: Correct sign/direction interpretation
description: Essential: The answer must state the direction is opposite to the initial velocity or use a negative sign appropriately.

title: Correct application of formula
description: Important: The student must use the average acceleration formula a = (v_final - v_initial) / time.

title: Correct velocity assignment
description: Important: The student must correctly assign v_initial = +10 m/s (towards ground) and v_final = -20 m/s (opposite direction) or vice versa with consistent sign convention.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The final answer should have correct units of m/s².

title: Time interval used
description: Important: The student must correctly use the given interaction time of 0.1 s in the calculation.

title: Sign error in subtraction
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student calculates (10 - (-20)) or similar, incorrectly handling the direction change, leading to a magnitude of 100 m/s².

title: Ignoring direction for magnitude
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student states the acceleration as -300 m/s² without acknowledging the magnitude is 300 m/s², or gives only the magnitude without direction/sign context.
